Title: Cards Wanted, Monocle and Rules Doctoring.

Messages.Author: S. Dembo
Messages.Body:
Ok, first of all, myopinion on the Monocle.
Its an obviously great card, but people read too much into it. It says
on the card that the person must answer truthfully. "Will you answer
affirmatvely to my next question?" Truthfully, I could not possibly
answer that question without knowing what the next one would be. If I
answered yes OR no, then I would not be giving an honest answer. <>shrugs<>

ANYWAY, here's a situation which I don't think too many people have
thought about yet. There is a Tremere who has the special ability to
transfer one blood from herself to any Tremere in the game. Well, what
I'm wondering is, can she transfer blood from herself to uncontrolled
vampires? No where on the card does it say that the Tremere she
transfers has to be ready, much less even controlled. SO, if she can,
then once you get a hunting ground out, she's either you're own personal
edge (put one on an uncontrolled trememere and slurp it off during
influence) or she's an infinitely cool version of Arcane Library!
Whatcha all think?

As to trading, I'm looking for the following cards:
Malkavian Madness Network
Kine Dominance
Soul Gem
Golconda
Freak Drive
Day Operation
Entrancement
Renegade Garou
Monocle of Clarity
Charnas the Imp

I have a ton of extra rares among them a large number of Justicar and
Praxis Seizures, Segnir Dagger, Blood Puppy, Fragment of the Book of Nod,
Fists of Death, Ghoul Escort, Tasha Morgan, Art Museum, Behind You,
Aaron's Feeding Razor, Dawn Ooperation
Gypsies, Thadius Zho, Temptation of a greater Power, and those are just
off the top of my head! Mail me if you're interested in doing some trading!

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
S. Dembo <sde...@blue.weeg.uiowa.edu> wrote:
>...There is a Tremere who has the special ability to

>transfer one blood from herself to any Tremere in the game. Well, what
>I'm wondering is, can she transfer blood from herself to uncontrolled
>vampires? No where on the card does it say that the Tremere she

>transfers has to be ready, much less even controlled...

Cards never interact with uncontrolled vampires unless they say they do;
Sabine (the vampire you're thinking of) doesn't say she can give blood
to uncontrolled Tremere, so can. Cards *can* interact freely with vampires
both ready and in torpor unless the card says otherwise; Sabine doesn't say
anything about that, so can transfer blood to any controlled vampire.

Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for
aa...@cats.ucsc.edu Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

Temper, temper...

> Yes, they *are* in the game. Ref: Rules section 11.1. The crypt and
> library are not defined in the play area, and are thus not "in the
> game," but the uncontrolled vampires are "in the game."

Perhaps a change in wording is in order. Try on "in play" instead of "in
the game." Certainly all of the cards in my deck, in my crypt, and in my
hand are "in the game," as are the glass beads I use for counters and the
piece of felt that I play on. However, not all of the cards are "in
play," specifically, those in my hand, those in my ash heap, those in my
deck, those vampires who are as of yet uncontrolled, and those vampires,
locations, and titles which are contested.

> If you plan on posting and telling me "no, they're not" without
> something to back up your statement, you might as well just save
> your bandwidth for someone who will listen.

Okay, here's some rules backup for you. Section 8 - Contested Cards: "If
your contested card is the only contested card not being yielded, you
turn it face up and move it into play, untapped, at the start of your
turn." Clearly these contested cards were "in the game," yet they were
"out of play." To add insult to injury, here's a snippet from section
12.4: "Putting Vampires into Play: At the end of the influence phase, a
vampire in your inactive region with as many blood counters on it as its
blood capacity becomes controlled, is turned right-side up, and is put
into the active region." So yes, those uncontrolled vampires are "in the
game," but they are not "in play."

Now go play whatever cheesy rules you want to and wave the rule booklet
and jump up and down. Put me in your kill file and have a nice day.

I believe there is a section in the rule book about bringing vampires into
play(or something like that in the index). In that section, it infers that
even though vamps in the crypt might be "in the game"(as are vamps created by
the embrace and vamps in the ash heap and also vamps that are being contested
at that same moment) the are not officially in play. My feeling is that the
people that wrote up sabine's card meant to say that she could transfer 1
blood to any vampire in play, but thats just my feeling.

Anyway with regards to vampires in the uncontrolled region, counters on them
do not, repeat do _not_ stand for health like blood on sabine does. Rather,
blood counters on uncontrolled vampires stands for influence placed on that
vamp to bring it under your control. Saying that sabine can trade one of her
health blood counters for an influence blood counter is slightly nonsensical.

Okay, let's take that for a sec. I'll buy that they're not in play,
especially given the good justification you've given. I suppose the
big question now is what good is defining "the playing area" if it
doesn't define vampires? This is more of a broken rules question.
If the uncontrolled area is defined as a play area, while the crypt
ash heap and library aren't, what's the difference between this area
and those others? There are cards that affect the crypt, cards that
affect libraries, and cards that affect uncontrolled vampires. Why
is the uncontrolled region defined differently?

The only card that seems to be worded as 'in the game' versus 'in
play' is Sabine, leading me to believe that she can be used on any
vampire, controlled or uncontrolled. This doesn't reconcile with
Tom's ruling on Sabine. So what I'm wondering is why the rules even
bother with making a distinction between the uncontrolled vampires
and the other stuff.
